newsitem.title: UK: Dixons hits year high on results comment.
newsitem.headline: Dixons hits year high on results comment.

text.p: Shares in Dixons Group Plc rose to their highest level of the year by mid-morning on Thursday amid positive analyst and press comment on the company's results released on Wednesday.

Defying losses elsewhere in the UK equity market, shares in the electrical retailer were up 12-1/2p at 549 by 0854 GMT -- after earlier reaching a high of 555p -- in trade of just over two million shares.
Dealers said BZW analysts raised the stock to a "buy" from a "hold" and other analysts were positive, after Dixons on Wednesday posted a 41 percent rise in yearly pre-tax profit to 190.2 million stg.
A 17 percent rise in same-store sales also helped spark a round of upgrades to analysts' profit forecasts.
Nick Bubb at SocGen said he set a short-term price target of 600p on the stock and said there could be more to go for beyond that.
"If they are delivering that sort of growth, then the stock's rating has been too low," Bubb said. "The quality of earnings has improved and there is digital TV to come."
Bubb said he expected pre-tax profit to rise to 240 million stg in the current year, putting the stock on a multiple of 14.5 times prospective earnings.
Earlier positive press comment on Dixons results helped spark early gains in the shares.

The Financial Times Lex column highlighted Dixons' 17 percent rise in same store sales and said the stock "looks set for a further leg-up," while the Tempus column in the Times said the stock's in-line rating was "ridiculous" given its growth rate.

Before yesterday's results, Dixons shares had underperformed the FTSE 100 index this year amid fears that rising UK interest rates would dampen consumer spending. Early this month the shares were trading near their lows of the year.
Dixons shares suffered a setback in January, after first-half results prompted a wave of profit-taking in the stock, which had risen sharply through 1996.
